route: The third blow-up level: realise B^3 (7-cube, height 22) and measure the cost of one level
headline: B^3 is NOT realised; but thm:blowup is relaxed (the parity is needed only along the walk, and z is free among the maximal-height translates, giving 2^21 x 4 admissible level-three targets of height 22), the blow-up's OUTER machinery is realised and verified from the game on 194 vertices (7 Max, 1 Min, denominator 2^10) — the first 7-cube realisation in this project — and the residual obstruction is localised to six explicit inner strategies at the coordinate alpha_2 of the translated layer.

results.name: b3:free-parity
results.statement: For ANY p : {0,1}^m -> {0,1} and ANY z in {0,1}^m, the modified blow-up B_{p,z}(s) (inner part s(v xor z) on layer (0,0) and s(v) elsewhere, outer part thm:blowup's table with p(v) in place of h(v) mod 2) is an acyclic unique sink orientation of the (m+2)-cube with sink (0,0,o xor z); and if p agrees with h mod 2 along the bottom-antipodal walk of s from u, its BA walk from (1,0,u) (h(u) even) or (0,1,u) (h(u) odd) has length exactly h(u)+2+h(o xor z). thm:blowup is the case p = h mod 2, z = o xor u.
results.argument: The USO and acyclicity arguments of thm:blowup use the parity only through four properties that BOTH columns of the outer table have: the four outer sets form a USO of the 2-cube; layer (0,0) gets the empty set; every other layer gets a coordinate on which it has a 1; and at fixed v the outer arcs among the three layers other than (0,0) form a directed path. Translation by any z is a cube automorphism, so the layer-(0,0) inner part is again an AUSO with sink o xor z, and the sink of B_{p,z}(s) is the unique vertex with empty outmap, namely (0,0,o xor z). For the height: p alternates along the walk of s from u, so each step flips both outer coordinates and advances the inner walk; after h(u) steps the walk is at (1,0,o); two more steps give (0,1,o) and (0,0,o); inside layer (0,0) the walk is, in the coordinates y = v xor z, the walk of s from o xor z, of length h(o xor z). CONSEQUENCE: for s = B^2 (h* = 10 at u in {12,14,28,30}, o = 4) there are 2^21 admissible p and z in {8,10,24,26}, ALL of BA height 22 — a 2^23-fold relaxation of the level-three target that thm:blowup did not expose.
results.verification: b3lib.py (blow_p), t_pt2.py: 2600 random admissible pairs (p,z) at m = 1, 3, 5 (seeds the 1-cube, B^1, B^2) — every one an AUSO with the predicted sink and BA height exactly h(u)+2+h(o xor z); 0 failures. t_ptilde.py: exhaustive over all 8 admissible p at m = 3, 0 failures. All integer arithmetic.

results.name: b3:translate
results.statement: For t(v) := s(v xor z): the edge direction satisfies g^t_i(v) = g_i(v xor z) for i not in z, and g^t_i(v) = - g_i(v xor (z minus {i})) for i in z. So translation by a single coordinate e_j REVERSES every j-edge and reads every other coordinate at the flipped sigma_j.
results.argument: g^t_i(v) = + iff bit i of s((v|_{i=0}) xor z) is 1. For i not in z, (v|_{i=0}) xor z = (v xor z)|_{i=0}. For i in z, (v|_{i=0}) xor z = (v xor (z minus {i}))|_{i=1}, and in a USO bit i of s(w|_{i=1}) is the complement of bit i of s(w|_{i=0}).
results.verification: t_l2exact.py: on B^2 (z = e_{beta_1}) the identity g_i on layer (0,0) = -g_i on layer (1,0) for i = beta_1 and = g_i at flipped beta_1 otherwise holds at all 8 inner strategies, exactly.

results.name: b3:b3
results.statement: B^3 = B(B^2) seeded at u = 12 has z = o xor u = 4 xor 12 = 8 = e_{alpha_2}, is an AUSO of the 7-cube of BA height 22 attained at 44,46,60,62,108,110,124,126, is not Holt-Klee, and has 28 forbidden (2-face, coordinate) pairs on 18 distinct 2-faces. Its walk from 44 is 44,83,45,81,40,80,32,71,33,69,36,68,4,27,5,25,0,24,8,15,9,13,12. The p-relaxed target B_{p,8}(B^2) used here has the same height and the same walk, is not Holt-Klee, and has only 16 forbidden pairs.
results.argument: Recomputed from B^2 with thm:blowup's rule; the full outmap is printed in the LaTeX and stored in B3.json / B3_targets.json.
results.verification: cube.py + t_b3.py + t_faces3.py: is_uso, is_acyclic, ba_heights, ba_trace, the unit-vertex-capacity Holt-Klee max-flow test and forbidden_pairs, all integer arithmetic; matches the paper's B^2 exactly.

results.name: b3:l2-design
results.statement: The design of prop:b2-realised, read off exactly: (i) action 0 of alpha_2 is (251/256)val(beta_2)+1/64 and action 0 of beta_2 is (509/512)val(alpha_2), so on layer (0,0) the outer pair is a CLOSED TWO-CYCLE with val(alpha_2) = Theta = 2048/3313 and val(beta_2) = 2036/3313 for all eight inner strategies, independently of the inner values (1 - AA' = 3313/131072); (ii) every inner row reads beta_2 (or the Min vertex, which reads beta_2) positively in exactly one action, so the inner values are in [0.4582,0.5538] on layer (0,0) against [0,0.4635] elsewhere, and val(beta_2) is 0.6145 there against at most 0.3476 elsewhere; (iii) the reversal of the translated coordinate beta_1 is driven by that change of scale against the constant -43/512 in its action-0 row.
results.argument: Direct exact computation from the published normal form; the numbers are exact rationals.
results.verification: t_l2exact.py, t_l2read.py, finalcheck.py (the 138-vertex game re-verified from the game: trap empty, outmap = B^2, nondegenerate, USO, acyclic, height 10, values increasing along the run).

results.name: b3:rise-sign
results.statement: In every nondegenerate stopping realisation of B_{p,e_j}(s): (a) val_{(0,0,v)} >= val_{(1,0,v)} and val_{(0,0,v)} >= val_{(0,1,v)} pointwise for every inner strategy v; (b) with w = p^{j,1} - p^{j,0}, sign(w . (val_{(0,0,v)} - val_{(1,0,v)})) = sign(Delta_j(val_{(0,0,v)})) = - sign(Delta_j(val_{(1,0,v)})); (c) hence w has entries of BOTH signs and the 2^m nonnegative rise vectors must lie on both sides of w-perp, split exactly according to g_j.
results.argument: (a) is lem:switch for the single improving switch {alpha} at (1,0,v) and {beta} at (0,1,v), both improving because the outer part of layer (1,0) always contains alpha and that of (0,1) always contains beta. (b) b3:translate reverses the j-edge between layer (0,0) and layer (1,0), and Delta_j is affine with linear part w. (c) if w >= 0 then by (a) every w.(rise) >= 0, so g_j would be constant on the inner cube, impossible for a coordinate of a USO of dimension >= 2.
results.verification: t_rise.py: on prop:b2-realised's game with j = beta_1, w = (267,187,0,0,56,-460)/512 has both signs, all eight rises are nonnegative, and w.(rise) is positive at v = 0,1,2,4,5,6 and negative at v = 3,7, matching the layer-(0,0) sign of Delta_{beta_1} at every v. Exact rationals.

results.name: b3:parity-readable
results.statement: (a) MEASURED (float LP, no Farkas certificate): no affine functional of the 32 value vectors of prop:b2-realised's game has sign = h_{B^2}(v) mod 2 at all 32 strategies (LP optimum 0) — the level-two analogue of cor:parity-unreadable. (b) PROVED: one does have that sign at the eleven strategies of the walk of B^2 from 12; the induced total function p = 00010111011000001111101101110001 differs from the true parity at exactly the six strategies 6,10,20,21,22,26, all off the walk, so by b3:free-parity it is admissible.
results.argument: (b) is witnessed exactly by the game of b3:tb, whose outer vertex alpha_3 realises that sign pattern in exact arithmetic. The LP margin 8.056e-4 (over functionals that are differences of two substochastic rows) is a float measurement. (a) is a float LP optimum of 0, hence measured, not proved.
results.verification: t_sep11.py, t_sep_all.py (both level-two realisations, all four maximal-height starts, same answer); the exact witness is TB_nf_D10.json / TB_GAME_D10.json.

results.name: b3:tb
results.statement: There is a nondegenerate stopping SSG on 194 vertices (7 Max, 1 Min, 184 average, 2 sinks), denominator 2^10, whose improvement outmap is B_{p,0}(B^2) for the p of b3:parity-readable: an AUSO of the 7-cube of BA height 12 whose all-switches run is 44,83,45,81,40,80,32,71,33,69,36,68,4 — the first twelve steps of the walk of B_{p,8}(B^2). Its normal form is the level-two normal form (entries doubled to denominator 1024) on x,alpha_1,beta_1,alpha_2,beta_2,c_min, together with alpha_3: (0,0,0,0,0,0,1021,0 | 2) and (0,0,549,335,0,0,0,0 | 0); beta_3: (0,0,0,0,0,1023,0,0 | 0) and (271,201,0,0,336,0,0,88 | 1), over (x,alpha_1,beta_1,alpha_2,beta_2,alpha_3,beta_3,c_min | t_1) in 1024-ths. This is the blow-up's outer machinery — the parity readout and the rest predicate — at a cost of +2 Max, +0 Min, +1 bit, +56 vertices over the level-two game, but WITH THE TRIVIAL TRANSLATION z = 0, so height h+2 and not 2h+2.
results.argument: Designed: the inner six vertices do not read alpha_3 or beta_3, so their values are the level-two values in all four layers and the inner outmap is B^2 on each; on layer (0,0) the outer pair is a closed two-cycle with A = 1021/1024, A' = 1023/1024, q = 1/512, Theta = 2048/4093, which makes both outer vertices at rest there; the two action-1 rows were fixed by the LP of b3:two-cycle and rounded to denominator 2^10.
results.verification: tb_build.py verifies the normal form exactly (all 128 value vectors as the minimum over the two Min strategies, verified fixed points of T_sigma, outmap, nondegeneracy, USO, acyclicity, height). tb_game.py builds the explicit fair-coin SSG (build.build_ssg) and verifies FROM THE GAME (verify.analyse, exact elimination, 256 profile values): greatest trap empty, out-degree two everywhere, outmap = B_{p,0}(B^2), nondegenerate, USO, acyclic, height 12, val_sigma nondecreasing at all 192 non-sink vertices along the run. Files TB_nf_D10.json, TB_GAME_D10.json.

results.name: b3:two-cycle
results.statement: If the outer pair carries the two-cycle rows A.val(beta)+q and A'.val(alpha) and the inner vertices do not read it (so the inner values z_v are fixed), the outer rule of b3:free-parity holds iff, with F := f - Ah - q and H := h - A'f for the two action-1 rows f,h, one has f(z_v) < Theta, h(z_v) < A'Theta, max(F,H) > 0 and F > 0 iff p(v) = 1 (F and H are never both positive). Consequently, for every pair with z_v >= z_{v'} componentwise, p(v) = 1, p(v') = 0: 1 - AA' < pi.(z_v - z_{v'}) / pi.(z_* - z_{v'}) <= max_j (z_v-z_{v'})_j/(z_*-z_{v'})_j, where pi >= 0 is f's coefficient vector and z_* = val dominates every z_v. The two-cycle must be almost lossless.
results.argument: Substituting the four layer values into Delta_alpha and Delta_beta gives f - Theta and (1-AA')f - q on the two layers with sigma_beta = 0 and the single expression F on the two with sigma_beta = 1, dually for beta; AH + F = (1-AA')f - q < 0 excludes both being positive. The inequality follows from F(z_v) > 0 >= ... > AA' f(z_{v'}) + q by monotonicity of h and H(z_{v'}) > 0, together with Theta - f(z_{v'}) >= f(z_*) - f(z_{v'}) = pi.(z_* - z_{v'}).
results.verification: tb2.py (the scan that found the feasible design) and an exact computation of the dominance-pair ratios: the pair (20,28) forces 1 - AA' < 78974227846783/2781927489443544 = 0.028389 and (16,8) forces < 0.031184; prop:b2-realised has 1 - AA' = 3313/131072 = 0.025276 (inside by ten per cent) and b3:tb has 4093/1048576 = 0.003903. All exact.

results.name: b3:theta-floor
results.statement: If the translated coordinate j and a second Max vertex j' carry the two-cycle rows, then at EVERY Max strategy with sigma_j = sigma_{j'} = 0, in every one of the four layers, val(j) = Theta = q/(1-AA') and val(j') = A'Theta, independently of everything else. Hence the action-1 readout Psi of j must exceed Theta at the 2^{m-2} such strategies of layer (0,0) and fall below it at the corresponding strategies of the other three layers (or vice versa where g_j = +): the layer-(0,0) rise must carry the readout across an ABSOLUTE threshold fixed by the previous level's outer pair, not merely reorder the values. For the published level-two rows Theta = 2048/3313 = 0.6182 while its own inner values never exceed 0.5538, so a level-three realisation on those rows must lift the readout of alpha_2 by at least 0.065 on layer (0,0) and by nothing on the other three.
results.argument: The two action-0 rows close on each other whatever the rest, giving the unique solution (Theta, A'Theta); the margin of j at such a strategy is Psi(val) - Theta, whose sign b3:translate reverses between layer (0,0) and the other three. Substochasticity of Psi and val <= 1 give the last clause.
results.verification: t_l2exact.py confirms val(alpha_2) = 2048/3313 at all eight layer-(0,0) strategies of the level-two game, exactly, and that the level-two inner values top out at 29188096000/52702783249 = 0.5538.

results.name: b3:decompose
results.statement: If action 0 of alpha reads only beta, action 0 of beta reads only alpha, action 1 of beta does not read alpha, and no vertex of I u Y reads alpha, then the values on I u Y depend on the layer only through the three classes {(0,0)}, {(1,0)}, {(0,1),(1,1)}, and on each class they are the values of the m-Max stopping SSG obtained from the rows of I u Y by substituting for val(beta) respectively the CONSTANT A'Theta, A'.Psi_alpha(.), and Psi_beta(.). So a realisation of B_{p,z}(s) is exactly: ONE family of rows on I u Y realising s o (+z) under the constant substitution and s under each of the other two, plus the outer conditions. This reduces the level-three design from 896 sign constraints to 3 x 160 + 128.
results.argument: On layer (0,0) the two action-0 rows close on each other; on (1,0) val(beta) = A'Psi_alpha; on (0,1) and (1,1) val(beta) = Psi_beta, which does not involve val(alpha). Since nothing in I u Y reads alpha, the equations for I u Y close once val(beta) is substituted, and the substituted system is a stopping SSG's fixed-point system with a unique solution (thm:contraction).
results.verification: t_decomp.py on prop:b2-realised's game: all four hypotheses hold; the inner value vectors on layers (0,1) and (1,1) are equal strategy by strategy; and the layer-(0,0) inner values are exactly those of the constant-substituted system. Exact rationals.

results.name: b3:rise-direction
results.statement: Under b3:decompose, at any inner strategy v where one Min strategy is a best response at both (0,0,v) and (0,1,v): val_{(0,0,v)} - val_{(0,1,v)} = (I - M_v)^{-1} b_v . (theta - Psi_beta(val_{(0,1,v)})), a NONNEGATIVE MULTIPLE of the single vector (I-M_v)^{-1}b_v >= 0, where M_v and b_v are the inner part and the beta-slot weights of the rows selected at v. Hence sign(w . rise) = sign(w . (I-M_v)^{-1} b_v), the transfer impedance from the new beta to the margin of the translated coordinate under the profile selected at v, and by b3:rise-sign it must follow g_j. In particular a design in which the selected profile does not change between the two layers can only reverse margins in ONE direction.
results.argument: Both value vectors solve y = M_v y + c_v + b_v s with the same M_v, c_v, b_v, with s = theta on layer (0,0) and s = Psi_beta(val_{(0,1,v)}) on layer (0,1); subtract and invert I - M_v (nonnegative inverse, the game being stopping). theta >= Psi_beta(val_{(0,1,v)}) by b3:rise-sign(a) at beta.
results.verification: t_riseform.py on prop:b2-realised's game (I u Y = {x,alpha_1,beta_1,c_min}, slot beta_2, j = beta_1, theta = 2036/3313): the identity holds EXACTLY at the six inner strategies 0,1,2,4,5,6 and fails at 3 and 7 — precisely the two at which the Min vertex changes its best response between layer (0,0) (action 0) and the other three (action 1), and precisely the two at which the reversal of Delta_{beta_1} goes in the hard direction + -> -. So the Min vertex of the level-two realisation is not a parity reader but a PROFILE SWITCH.

results.name: b3:residue
results.statement: Twelve independent sequential-LP runs on the b3:decompose reduction with z = e_{alpha_2} (104 parameters, 320 constraints) bring the count down to 10 wrong, and every one of the six best runs has the SAME six in its residue: the coordinate alpha_2 in the constant-substituted system at the inner strategies 17,19,23,25,27,31 — exactly {g^{B^2}_{alpha_2} = +} = {sigma_{beta_2} = 1 and h_{B^1}(sigma_x,sigma_{alpha_1},sigma_{beta_1}) odd}, the level-two parity readout itself. All 26 reversals in the direction - -> + are found; the six in the direction + -> - are not. At the best point Psi_beta has collapsed to the zero map and all slot weights are below 0.05: the search settles on the PURE BOOST, which by b3:rise-direction can reverse in one direction only, and never finds the profile-switch configuration that the level-two game uses.
results.argument: Search output, not a proof; the full 896-constraint search (n = 8,9,10, every admissible z, warm-started at b3:tb and at random) left between 30 and 76 constraints unsatisfied, with 28 of the best run's 30 failures in layer (0,0) on beta_1, alpha_2, beta_2.
results.verification: stageA.py / stageB.py (the reduction), diagA.py (the residue), diag3.py (the full search residue), stageA_best.json (the best point, its rows and its residue), logs/A_z*.log, logs/B_k*.log, logs/b_z*.log.

gap: There is a family of substochastic dyadic rows on five Max vertices (x, alpha_1, beta_1, alpha_2, beta_2) and k Min vertices, each row carrying in addition a weight on a "beta_3 slot", together with a constant theta in (0,1) and a substochastic affine map Psi_beta and a substochastic affine map Psi_alpha of the five Max values, such that substituting theta for the slot yields a nondegenerate stopping system whose improvement outmap is B^2 composed with (xor e_{alpha_2}), while substituting Psi_beta and substituting A'.Psi_alpha each yield one whose improvement outmap is B^2 — equivalently (b3:decompose), there is a nondegenerate stopping SSG with seven Max vertices whose improvement outmap is B_{p,e_{alpha_2}}(B^2) for some p agreeing with h_{B^2} mod 2 along the bottom-antipodal walk of B^2 from 12.
next_steps: (1) Attack the gap in the b3:decompose form (stageA.py / stageB.py in the code directory are the exact harness; the best point is stageA_best.json, 10 wrong of 320) with the Min response PRESCRIBED rather than computed: by b3:min-role the level-two game reverses the hard direction only where its Min vertex changes response between the layers, so prescribe tau_C and tau_B to differ at exactly the six strategies 17,19,23,25,27,31 and impose tau's optimality as explicit linear constraints (the round-15 gadget route's slp6.py does this at m = 5). Every search so far collapsed to the pure boost (Psi_beta = 0), which b3:rise-direction proves cannot reverse both ways. (2) Use the OTHER freedom b3:free-parity exposes and that this route did not spend: the level-two orientation itself may be replaced by B_{p_1,z_1}(B^1) for any of the 2^3 admissible p_1 and z_1 in {4,6} — sixteen 5-cube AUSOs of height 10, each with its own translated coordinate at level three; realise one of them whose alpha_2-analogue has a row shape that can reverse (b3:theta-floor says the two-cycle shape forces a crossing of an absolute threshold, which is what blocks the published rows). (3) Either way, decide the question of rem:blowup-realise for the third level: the outer half is now known to be additive (+2 Max, +0 Min, +1 bit), so the whole cost question is the cost of the translation. (4) A negative result would also be worth having: prove that no family of rows can satisfy b3:rise-sign(c) at level three with k = 1, which by b3:rise-direction is a statement about the sign pattern of the transfer impedances w.(I-M_v)^{-1}b_v across the 32 selected profiles.

%  Route b3 : the third blow-up level.  Paste-ready, amsthm style.
%  Full file: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/b3-level/b3.tex

\begin{lemma}[What a translation does to an outmap]\label{b3:translate}
Let $s$ be an outmap of the $m$-cube, $z\in\{0,1\}^{m}$, and
$t(v):=s(v\oplus z)$. Write $g_i(v)=+$ when the $i$-edge at $v$ points from
$v_i=0$ to $v_i=1$ (a function of $v_{-i}$ alone). Then for $i\notin z$,
$g^{t}_i(v)=g_i(v\oplus z)$, and for $i\in z$,
$g^{t}_i(v)=-\,g_i(v\oplus(z\setminus\{i\}))$. In particular translation by a
single coordinate $e_j$ \emph{reverses every $j$-edge} and leaves every other
coordinate's edge direction unchanged except that it is read at the flipped
$\sigma_j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$g^t_i(v)=+$ iff bit $i$ of $t(v|_{i=0})=s((v|_{i=0})\oplus z)$ is $1$. If
$i\notin z$ then $(v|_{i=0})\oplus z=(v\oplus z)|_{i=0}$, giving the first
clause. If $i\in z$ then $(v|_{i=0})\oplus z=(v\oplus(z\setminus\{i\}))|_{i=1}$,
and in a unique sink orientation bit $i$ of $s(w|_{i=1})$ is the complement of
bit $i$ of $s(w|_{i=0})$, whence the sign change.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The blow-up needs the parity only along the walk]\label{b3:free-parity}
Let $s$ be an acyclic unique sink orientation of the $m$-cube with sink $o$ and
height function $h$. Let $p:\{0,1\}^{m}\to\{0,1\}$ be \emph{any} function and
$z\in\{0,1\}^{m}$ \emph{any} vector. Define $B_{p,z}(s)$ on the
$(m+2)$-cube exactly as in \Cref{thm:blowup}, with inner part $s(v\oplus z)$ on
the layer $(\alpha,\beta)=(0,0)$ and $s(v)$ elsewhere, and outer part
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
   (\alpha,\beta) & p(v)=0 & p(v)=1\\ \hline
   (0,0) & \emptyset & \emptyset\\
   (1,0) & \{\alpha,\beta\} & \{\alpha\}\\
   (0,1) & \{\beta\} & \{\alpha,\beta\}\\
   (1,1) & \{\alpha\} & \{\beta\}
 \end{array}
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $B_{p,z}(s)$ is an acyclic unique sink orientation of the $(m+2)$-cube,
      with sink $(0,0,o\oplus z)$, for every $p$ and every $z$;
\item if $u$ is a vertex and $p(w)\equiv h(w)\pmod 2$ at every vertex $w$ of
      the bottom-antipodal walk of $s$ from $u$, then the bottom-antipodal
      walk of $B_{p,z}(s)$ from $(1,0,u)$ (if $h(u)$ is even) or $(0,1,u)$ (if
      $h(u)$ is odd) has length exactly $h(u)+2+h(o\oplus z)$, so
      $h^{\ast}(B_{p,z}(s))\ge h(u)+2+h(o\oplus z)$.
\end{enumerate}
\Cref{thm:blowup} is the case $p=h\bmod 2$, $z=o\oplus u$ with $h(u)$ maximal.
Taking $u$ and $o\oplus z$ both of maximal height gives height $\ge 2h^{\ast}(s)+2$
as there, but leaves $p$ free at the $2^{m}-h(u)-1$ vertices off the walk and
$z$ free among $\{o\oplus u':h(u')=h^{\ast}(s)\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(a) Translation by $z$ is an automorphism of the cube, so $v\mapsto s(v\oplus z)$
is again an acyclic unique sink orientation, with sink $o\oplus z$. The three
verifications in the proof of \Cref{thm:blowup} use the parity only through the
following four properties of the displayed table, each of which holds for both
of its columns and hence for every $p$: the four outer sets form a unique sink
orientation of the $2$-cube (Szab\'o--Welzl on all six pairs); the layer $(0,0)$
receives $\emptyset$; each layer $L\ne(0,0)$ receives a coordinate on which $L$
has a $1$; and, at a fixed $v$, the outer arcs among the three layers
$\ne(0,0)$ form a directed path. The unique-sink argument, the acyclicity
argument and the identification of the sink are then verbatim those of
\Cref{thm:blowup}: no outer edge leaves layer $(0,0)$, so a cycle meeting it
lies in it and contradicts the acyclicity of the translate; a cycle avoiding it
projects to a closed directed walk of $s$, hence to a constant $v$, and at a
fixed $v$ a directed path carries no cycle. The sink is the unique vertex whose
outmap is empty, that is layer $(0,0)$ with $s(v\oplus z)=\emptyset$, namely
$v=o\oplus z$.

(b) Along the walk of $s$ from $u$ the height drops by one per step, so $p$
alternates on it. At $(1,0,w)$ with $p(w)=0$ the outmap is
$\{\alpha,\beta\}\cup s(w)$, so one step gives $(0,1,w\oplus s(w))$, whose
inner vertex is the next vertex of the walk and has the other parity; at
$(0,1,w')$ with $p(w')=1$ the outmap is again $\{\alpha,\beta\}\cup s(w')$ and
the step returns to layer $(1,0)$. After $h(u)$ steps the inner vertex is $o$
and the layer is $(1,0)$ in both cases. There $p(o)=0$ and $s(o)=\emptyset$
give the step to $(0,1,o)$, where the outmap is $\{\beta\}$ and the step goes
to $(0,0,o)$. Inside layer $(0,0)$ the outer part is empty and the walk is, in
the coordinates $y:=v\oplus z$, the bottom-antipodal walk of $s$ from
$y=o\oplus z$, of length $h(o\oplus z)$, ending at $y=o$, that is at the sink
$(0,0,o\oplus z)$.
\end{proof}

      $\beta_2$) with a positive weight in exactly one of its two actions, so

\begin{lemma}[The reversed coordinate reads the rise]\label{b3:rise-sign}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping SSG realising $B_{p,e_j}(s)$ with
$\Vmax=\{$inner$\}\cup\{\alpha,\beta\}$. For an inner strategy $v$ put
$y_v:=\val_{(0,0,v)}$, $x_v:=\val_{(1,0,v)}$ and $x'_v:=\val_{(0,1,v)}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $y_v\ge x_v$ and $y_v\ge x'_v$ pointwise on all of $V$, for every $v$ ---
      $\alpha$ is switchable at $(1,0,v)$ and switching it gives $(0,0,v)$,
      $\beta$ is switchable at $(0,1,v)$ and switching it gives $(0,0,v)$
      (\Cref{lem:switch});
\item with $w:=p^{j,1}-p^{j,0}$ the coefficient vector of the reversed
      coordinate's margin $\Delta_j$, one has
      $\operatorname{sign}\bigl(w\cdot(y_v-x_v)\bigr)
      =\operatorname{sign}\Delta_j(y_v)=-\operatorname{sign}\Delta_j(x_v)$ for
      every $v$;
\item consequently $w$ has entries of both signs, and the $2^{m}$ rise vectors
      $y_v-x_v\ge0$ are split by the hyperplane $w^{\perp}$ exactly according
      to the edge direction $g_j$ of $s$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) is \Cref{lem:switch} for the single switches $\{\alpha\}$ at $(1,0,v)$ and
$\{\beta\}$ at $(0,1,v)$, both improving because the outer part of the layer
$(1,0)$ always contains $\alpha$ and that of $(0,1)$ always contains $\beta$.
(b) By \Cref{b3:translate} the $j$-edge is reversed between
the layer $(0,0)$ and the layer $(1,0)$, so $\Delta_j(y_v)$ and $\Delta_j(x_v)$
have opposite signs; $\Delta_j$ is affine with linear part $w$, so
$\Delta_j(y_v)-\Delta_j(x_v)=w\cdot(y_v-x_v)$ has the sign of $\Delta_j(y_v)$.
(c) If $w\ge0$ then $w\cdot(y_v-x_v)\ge0$ for all $v$ by (a), so $\Delta_j(y_v)>0$
for all $v$ and $g_j$ is constant on the inner cube, which no coordinate of a
unique sink orientation of dimension $\ge2$ has. Dually for $w\le0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Checked on \Cref{prop:b2-realised}'s game with $j=\beta_1$: $w=\tfrac1{512}
(267,187,0,0,56,-460)$, the eight rises are nonnegative, and
$w\cdot(y_v-x_v)$ is positive at $v=0,1,2,4,5,6$ and negative at $v=3,7$,
matching the layer-$(0,0)$ sign of $\Delta_{\beta_1}$ at every $v$.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[A valid parity is affinely readable; the true one is not]\label{b3:parity-readable}

\begin{lemma}[The layer-$(0,0)$ two-cycle must be almost lossless]\label{b3:two-cycle}
Suppose a realisation has, as in \Cref{b3:l2-design}(i) and \Cref{b3:tb}, an
outer pair whose action-$0$ rows are $A\val(\beta)+q$ and $A'\val(\alpha)$ with
$A,A',q>0$, and suppose the inner vertices do not read the outer pair, so that
the inner values $z_v$ are fixed. Write $f,h$ for the two action-$1$ rows, both
substochastic affine (hence monotone) in $z$, and $\Theta:=q/(1-AA')$. Then the
outer rule of \Cref{b3:free-parity} holds iff, writing $F:=f-Ah-q$ and
$H:=h-A'f$, for every $v$
\[
 f(z_v)<\Theta,\qquad h(z_v)<A'\Theta,\qquad
 \max\bigl(F(z_v),H(z_v)\bigr)>0,\qquad
 F(z_v)>0\iff p(v)=1 ;
\]
$F$ and $H$ are never both positive. Consequently, for every pair of
inner strategies with $z_v\ge z_{v'}$ componentwise, $p(v)=1$ and $p(v')=0$,
\[
  1-AA'\;<\;\frac{\pi\cdot(z_v-z_{v'})}{\pi\cdot(z_{\ast}-z_{v'})}
  \;\le\;\max_{j\,:\,(z_\ast-z_{v'})_j>0}\frac{(z_v-z_{v'})_j}{(z_{\ast}-z_{v'})_j},
\]
where $\pi\ge0$ is the coefficient vector of $f$ and $z_{\ast}=\val$ is the
value vector of the optimal strategy, which dominates all the others; if the
denominator vanishes the design is infeasible. On the level-two configuration
and the $p$ of \Cref{b3:parity-readable} the pair $(v,v')=(20,28)$ forces
$1-AA'<\tfrac{78974227846783}{2781927489443544}=0.028389$ and the pair
$(16,8)$ forces $1-AA'<0.031184$; \Cref{prop:b2-realised} has
$1-AA'=3313/131072=0.025276$ --- inside the bound by ten per cent --- and
\Cref{b3:tb} has $1-AA'=4093/1048576=0.003903$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the layer $(0,0)$ the two action-$0$ rows close on each other, so
$\val(\alpha)=\Theta$ and $\val(\beta)=A'\Theta$ there; on the layer $(1,0)$,
$\val(\alpha)=f$, $\val(\beta)=A'f$; on $(0,1)$, $\val(\beta)=h$,
$\val(\alpha)=Ah+q$; on $(1,1)$, $\val(\alpha)=f$ and $\val(\beta)=h$.
Substituting into $\Delta_\alpha=f-A\val(\beta)-q$ and
$\Delta_\beta=h-A'\val(\alpha)$ gives $\Delta_\alpha=f-\Theta$ on the layer
$(0,0)$ and $\Delta_\alpha=(1-AA')f-q$ on the layer $(1,0)$ --- using
$\Theta=AA'\Theta+q$ --- both negative exactly when $f<\Theta$, and
$\Delta_\alpha=F$ on both layers with $\sigma_\beta=1$, the same expression in
both, as the rule requires; dually $\Delta_\beta=h-A'\Theta$ on $(0,0)$ and
$(1-AA')h-A'q$ on $(0,1)$, both negative exactly when $h<A'\Theta$, and
$\Delta_\beta=H$ on both layers with $\sigma_\alpha=1$. Since
$AH+F=(1-AA')f-q<0$ under the first condition, $F$ and $H$ are never both
positive. For the inequality: $F(z_v)>0$ gives
$f(z_v)>Ah(z_v)+q\ge Ah(z_{v'})+q>AA'f(z_{v'})+q$ by monotonicity of $h$ and
$H(z_{v'})>0$; writing $f(z_v)-f(z_{v'})=\pi\cdot(z_v-z_{v'})$ and
$\Theta-f(z_{v'})\ge f(z_{\ast})-f(z_{v'})=\pi\cdot(z_{\ast}-z_{v'})$ (using
$f(z_{\ast})<\Theta$) turns it into the displayed bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The translation must cross a fixed threshold]\label{b3:theta-floor}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping SSG realising $B_{p,e_{j}}(s)$, and suppose
the translated coordinate $j$ and one further Max vertex $j'$ carry the
two-cycle rows of \Cref{b3:l2-design}(i): action $0$ of $j$ is
$A\val(j')+q$ and action $0$ of $j'$ is $A'\val(j)$, with $A,A',q>0$ and no
other targets. Then at every Max strategy $\sigma$ with
$\sigma_{j}=\sigma_{j'}=0$ --- in every one of the four layers ---
\[
  \val_\sigma(j)=\Theta:=\frac{q}{1-AA'},\qquad \val_\sigma(j')=A'\Theta ,
\]
independently of all the other values. Writing $\Psi$ for the action-$1$ row of
$j$, the reversal of the $j$-edges on the layer $(0,0)$ (\Cref{b3:translate})
forces
\[
 \Psi(\val_{(0,0,v)})>\Theta \quad\text{and}\quad \Psi(\val_{(L,v)})<\Theta
 \quad (L\ne(0,0))
\]
for every one of the $2^{m-2}$ inner strategies $v$ with $v_j=v_{j'}=0$ at
which $g_j=-$ in $s$, and the two inequalities exchanged where $g_j=+$. Since
$\Psi$ is substochastic, $\Psi>\Theta$ needs some vertex read by $\Psi$ to have
value $>\Theta$: the layer-$(0,0)$ rise of \Cref{b3:rise-sign} must carry the
readout across an \emph{absolute} threshold fixed by the two rows of the
previous level's outer pair, not merely reorder the values. For the published
level-two realisation this threshold is $\Theta=\tfrac{2048}{3313}=0.6182$
while its own inner values never exceed $0.5538$; so in a level-three
realisation built on those rows the inner vertices must read the new outer pair
$(\alpha_3,\beta_3)$ hard enough to lift the readout of $\alpha_2$ by at least
$0.065$ on the layer $(0,0)$ and by nothing at all on the other three.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On the layer of $\sigma$ the two action-$0$ rows close on each other, so
$\val_\sigma(j)=A\val_\sigma(j')+q$ and $\val_\sigma(j')=A'\val_\sigma(j)$,
whose unique solution is the displayed pair ($AA'<1$ because the rows are
substochastic and the game is stopping). The margin of $j$ at such a $\sigma$
is $\Psi(\val_\sigma)-\Theta$, and its sign is $g_j$, which
\Cref{b3:translate} reverses between the layer $(0,0)$ and the other three.
The last clause is $|p|_1+q\le1$ and $\val\le1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A level splits into three systems with one set of rows]\label{b3:decompose}
Let $G$ be a stopping SSG with $\Vmax=I\cup\{\alpha,\beta\}$, $|I|=m$, and
$\Vmin=Y$, whose rows satisfy: action $0$ of $\alpha$ reads only $\beta$ and
the sinks; action $0$ of $\beta$ reads only $\alpha$ and the sinks; action $1$
of $\beta$ does not read $\alpha$; and no vertex of $I\cup Y$ reads $\alpha$.
Write $\Psi_\alpha,\Psi_\beta$ for the action-$1$ rows of $\alpha,\beta$, and
$A,A',q$ as in \Cref{b3:two-cycle}. Then for every Max strategy $(L,v)$ the
values on $I\cup Y$ depend on the layer $L$ only through the three classes
$\{(0,0)\}$, $\{(1,0)\}$, $\{(0,1),(1,1)\}$, and on each class they are the
values of the $m$-Max stopping SSG obtained from the rows of $I\cup Y$ by
substituting for $\val(\beta)$, respectively,
\[
  A'\Theta \ \ (\text{a constant}),\qquad A'\Psi_\alpha(\cdot),\qquad
  \Psi_\beta(\cdot).
\]
Consequently a realisation of $B_{p,z}(s)$ by such a $G$ is exactly: one family
of rows on $I\cup Y$ which, under the constant substitution, realises
$s\circ(\oplus z)$ and, under each of the other two substitutions, realises
$s$; together with the outer conditions on $\alpha,\beta$. The game of
\Cref{prop:b2-realised} satisfies all four hypotheses, and its inner value
vectors on the layers $(0,1)$ and $(1,1)$ are indeed equal, strategy by
strategy.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On the layer $(0,0)$ the two action-$0$ rows close on each other
(\Cref{b3:theta-floor}), giving $\val(\beta)=A'\Theta$ whatever the rest; on
$(1,0)$, $\val(\alpha)=\Psi_\alpha$ and $\val(\beta)=A'\val(\alpha)$; on
$(0,1)$ and $(1,1)$, $\val(\beta)=\Psi_\beta$, which does not involve
$\val(\alpha)$. Since no vertex of $I\cup Y$ reads $\alpha$, the equations for
$I\cup Y$ close once $\val(\beta)$ is substituted, and the substituted system
is a stopping SSG's fixed-point system, whose solution is unique
(\Cref{thm:contraction}); the improvement outmap of $G$ restricted to a layer
is that of the substituted system.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The rise has one direction per selected profile]\label{b3:rise-direction}
Assume the hypotheses of \Cref{b3:decompose} and let $v$ be an inner strategy
at which one Min strategy is a best response both at $(0,0,v)$ and at
$(0,1,v)$. Let $M_v$ be the inner part and $b_v\ge0$ the vector of
$\beta$-slot weights of the rows selected at $v$. Then
\[
  \val_{(0,0,v)}|_{I\cup Y}-\val_{(0,1,v)}|_{I\cup Y}
  \;=\;(I-M_v)^{-1}b_v\cdot\bigl(\theta-\Psi_\beta(\val_{(0,1,v)})\bigr),
\]
a \emph{nonnegative multiple of the single vector} $(I-M_v)^{-1}b_v\ge0$. Hence
for the translated coordinate $j$, with $w=p^{j,1}-p^{j,0}$ restricted to
$I\cup Y$,
\[
  \operatorname{sign}\bigl(w\cdot(\val_{(0,0,v)}-\val_{(0,1,v)})\bigr)
  =\operatorname{sign}\bigl(w\cdot(I-M_v)^{-1}b_v\bigr),
\]
the sign of the transfer impedance from the new $\beta$ to the margin of $j$
under the profile selected at $v$; by \Cref{b3:rise-sign} it must follow $g_j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Both value vectors solve $y=M_vy+c_v+b_v\cdot s$ with the same $M_v,c_v,b_v$,
with $s=\theta$ on the layer $(0,0)$ and $s=\Psi_\beta(\val_{(0,1,v)})$ on the
layer $(0,1)$ --- the latter because $\val_{(0,1,v)}(\beta)=\Psi_\beta$
evaluated at that same vector. Subtracting and inverting $I-M_v$, which is
invertible with nonnegative inverse because the game is stopping, gives the
displayed identity; $\theta\ge\Psi_\beta(\val_{(0,1,v)})$ by
\Cref{b3:rise-sign}(a) applied to the vertex $\beta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[measured: this is what the Min vertex is for]\label{b3:min-role}
On \Cref{prop:b2-realised}'s game, with $I\cup Y=\{x,\alpha_1,\beta_1,c_{\min}\}$,
the slot $\beta_2$, $j=\beta_1$ and $\theta=\tfrac{2036}{3313}$, the identity of
\Cref{b3:rise-direction} holds \emph{exactly} at the six inner strategies
$0,1,2,4,5,6$ and fails at $3$ and $7$ --- precisely the two at which the Min
vertex changes its best response between the layer $(0,0)$ (action $0$) and the
other three (action $1$), and precisely the two at which the reversal of
$\Delta_{\beta_1}$ goes in the direction $+\to-$. At the other six,
$w\cdot(I-M_v)^{-1}b_v>0$ carries the easy direction $-\to+$. So in that
realisation the Min vertex is not a parity reader but a \emph{profile
switch}: it changes $M_v$ between the two layers exactly where a fixed rise
direction could not reverse the margin.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The residue of the search, localised]\label{b3:residue}
Run on the reduction of \Cref{b3:decompose} with $z=e_{\alpha_2}$ --- twelve
independent sequential-linear-programming runs over the $104$ parameters ---
the search brings the $320$ constraints down to $10$ wrong, and every one of
the six best runs has the same six in its residue: the coordinate
$\alpha_2$ in the constant-substituted system at the inner strategies
$17,19,23,25,27,31$. Those six are exactly $\{g^{B^{2}}_{\alpha_2}=+\}$, that is
$\{\sigma_{\beta_2}=1\ \text{and}\ h_{B^{1}}(\sigma_x,\sigma_{\alpha_1},
\sigma_{\beta_1})\ \text{odd}\}$: the level-two parity readout itself. The
$26$ reversals in the direction $-\to+$ are found; the six in the direction
$+\to-$ are not. At the best point $\Psi_\beta$ has collapsed to the zero map
and all the slot weights are below $0.05$: the search settles on the
\emph{pure boost}, which by \Cref{b3:rise-direction} can reverse margins in one
direction only. No run found a configuration of the kind the level-two game
uses (\Cref{b3:min-role}). Whether that is possible at level three is the open
point; nothing here excludes it.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The gap]\label{b3:gap}
The construction of \Cref{b3:tb} realises the blow-up's outer machinery ---
two Max vertices, no new Min vertex, one further bit of precision, $54$ further
average vertices --- but with the trivial translation $z=0$, so its height is
$h^{\ast}(B^{2})+2=12$ and not $2h^{\ast}(B^{2})+2=22$. What is missing is
exactly the layer-$(0,0)$ translation: by \Cref{b3:translate} the coordinate
$\alpha_2$ must have all $32$ of its margins reversed on that layer while the
other four inner coordinates are read at the flipped $\sigma_{\alpha_2}$, which
is $84$ of the $896$ sign constraints for $z=8$ (respectively $64$ for $z=24$,
both of height $22$). A sequential-linear-programming search over the
$2n(n+1)$ entries of the normal form, warm-started at \Cref{b3:tb} and at
random, with $n=8,9,10$ and every admissible $z$, left between $30$ and $76$
constraints unsatisfied; in the best runs $28$ of the $30$ residual failures
lie in the layer $(0,0)$, on the coordinates $\beta_1,\alpha_2,\beta_2$. No
obstruction is proved: \Cref{b3:rise-sign,b3:two-cycle,b3:theta-floor,%
b3:rise-direction} are necessary conditions that the level-two realisation
satisfies and that nothing here shows to be unsatisfiable at level three.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The cost of a level, as far as it is established]\label{b3:cost}
\[
\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c|c|c}
 & \dim & h & |\Vmax| & |\Vmin| & \text{denominator} & N\\ \hline
 B^{1} & 3 & 4 & 3 & 0 & 2^{6} & 58\ \text{(re-verified here; $39$ in \Cref{prop:m3-realised})}\\
 B^{2} & 5 & 10 & 5 & 1 & 2^{9} & 138\ \text{(\Cref{prop:b2-realised})}\\

The step $B^{1}\to B^{2}$ cost $+2$ Max, $+1$ Min, $+3$ bits, $+80$ vertices.
The outer half of the step $B^{2}\to B_{p,0}(B^{2})$ cost $+2$ Max, $+0$ Min,
$+1$ bit, $+56$ vertices --- additive, as \Cref{rem:blowup-realise} asks --- but
it buys only $h+2$, not $2h+2$. Whether the translation can be bought at
additive cost is exactly what remains open; the two data points $B^{1},B^{2}$
are all the evidence there is, and they are consistent with both an additive
and a multiplicative law.
\end{remark}
